headline: Threadit Thread of '3 AM Realizations' Causes Mass Existential Crisis
subheadline: Post accumulates 10,000 comments of increasingly disturbing observations
summary: A Threadit thread asking users to share thoughts they only have late at night has left thousands unable to sleep.
content:
A Threadit post titled "What's something you only realize at 3 AM?" has been blamed for what users are calling "a community-wide existential event."

The post, submitted to r/AskThreadit by u/CantSleepWontSleep, invited users to share the thoughts that only occur in the middle of the night. It has since accumulated over 10,000 comments and an unknown number of sleepless nights.

Top responses include:

- "Every photo of you is a photo of you in the past" (8,400 upvotes)
- "The last time your parents picked you up, and they put you down, and that was the last time, and neither of you knew" (7,200 upvotes)
- "Your stomach thinks all potatoes are mashed" (6,800 upvotes)
- "Someone out there has a video of you in the background of their vacation and you're acting weird" (5,900 upvotes)
- "The you from 10 years ago would think you have your life together right now" (5,100 upvotes)

Psychologists have weighed in on the phenomenon. "These are called 'intrusive thoughts' and they're normal," explained Dr. Patricia Huang. "What's not normal is 10,000 people sharing them simultaneously. That's how you create a collective spiral."

One comment, posted by u/TemporalDread at exactly 3:47 AM, simply read: "The last time you talked to some of your friends and didn't know it was the last time." It received 847 awards and crashed the Threadit mobile app for several hours.

"I read that thread at midnight," reported user u/RegretThisAlready. "It is now 6 AM. I have not slept. I have called everyone I know. Several of them were also reading the thread. We're all just on the phone together now, not talking."

The original poster has since edited the post to add: "I am so sorry."

A second edit, added at 4:17 AM, reads: "Actually no I'm not. Someone had to say it. Your tongue rests somewhere in your mouth and now you're aware of it."
author: Marcus Webb, Internet Culture Correspondent
